newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia 96 primary aluminium export seen 2.37 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia 96 primary aluminium export seen 2.37 mln T.

text.p: Russia's total exports of primary aluminium in 1996 will total 2.37 million tonnes compared to 1995's 2.11 million tonnes, the Kontsern Alyuminiy producers' association said on Monday.
It said that exports of aluminium products, which are not included in the above figures, would more than halve to 180,000 tonnes this year from last year's 386,000 tonnes.
The data, issued in a news release, was confirmed by Kontsern Alyuminiy's Yuri Dvinin, who said Kontsern Alyuminiy general director Igor Prokopov had prepared the release.
Dvinin said domestic producers had brought 70,000 tonnes of capacity back on line out of a total 150,000 tonnes idled under a two-year global output cutting deal which ended last spring.
But he said the remaining capacity would not be brought on line due to weak world prices. "This is in our interests and in the interests of the world market," he said.
He said Russian producers would see little reason to expand production capacity before the year 2000, when he expected domestic demand to pick up as the economy staged a comeback.
Kontsern Alyuminiy represents Russia's leading aluminium smelters. But some independent analysts have questioned the extent to which it actually reflects smelters' actual plans.
Dvinin said Russia would exchange data with the former participants of the expired Memorandum of Understanding global output cutting deal to plan output and export levels.
